response: Yes, short-term treatment with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can cause rebound aggravation of symptoms. This is known as rebound acid hypersecretion, where the stomach produces more acid than usual after stopping PPIs. Studies have shown that taking PPIs for a short period (usually 2-8 weeks) can lead to an increase in gastric acid secretion after discontinuation, resulting in worsened symptoms such as heartburn, acid reflux, and dyspepsia. This rebound effect is usually temporary, but it can be uncomfortable for patients and may lead to prolonged use of PPIs.
